frameworks.name: Revenue Per Square Foot Analysis
frameworks.definition: A diagnostic framework that identifies the highest-margin service category within a multi-service location, then extracts and replicates that core model across multiple smaller facilities rather than scaling the entire location.

frameworks.name: Alloy Semi-Private Training Model
frameworks.definition: A service-bundling model where three instructors deliver semi-private (1-on-4) training in 1,200 sq ft, generating $560k top-line revenue with 50% net margins, creating a replicable micro-unit that scales across multiple locations.

claims.text: Physical space (supply constraint) is the binding constraint blocking the tennis facility from scaling from $3M to $10M revenue, not pricing, offer, or sales process. Alex Hormozi confirmed this when the business owner stated inability to find enough space.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Does not apply to software or virtual service businesses
Does not apply to businesses where demand is below capacity

claims.text: Before scaling a multi-service facility, the founder should audit revenue per square foot across each service category to identify the highest-performing core engine, then replicate that isolated model across multiple smaller facilities rather than attempting to scale the entire multi-service location.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: High-margin service categories can operate in smaller footprints, making them easier to find and replicate across markets.
bounded_by: Does not apply to single-service businesses
Does not apply to businesses unable to isolate margin variation by category

examples.text: Rick Mayo founded Alloy, a fitness facility with one flagship location generating $3-4M annually from 8,000 sq ft through a portfolio of services: juice bar, personal training, semi-private group classes (1-on-4 format), and full group classes. When preparing to franchise the model, Mayo analyzed each service category for revenue per square foot and customer acquisition cost (CAC) to lifetime value (LTV) ratio. He discovered that semi-private training (3 instructors serving 1-on-4 classes) had the highest revenue-per-square-foot and the lowest CAC-to-LTV ratio. He extracted this service as the core replicable unit, which could operate in just 1,200 sq ft with $560k top-line revenue and 50% net margins, and this became the franchisable model rather than attempting to replicate the entire multi-service flagship.

The tennis facility owner operated a three-court facility previously with approximately 45% margins, indicating higher profitability in a smaller format. The owner currently manages a 45,000 sq ft facility generating $3M revenue with only 22% margins, suggesting the scaling from micro to flagship format sacrificed unit economics and may have been the wrong architectural decision. This contrasts with the Alloy case where the replicable micro model outperformed the larger facility on a per-square-foot basis.

practices.text: Audit revenue per square foot by service category within a multi-service facility before deciding on expansion strategy.
Increase pricing on high-demand service categories as an immediate lever to improve margins and profit when capacity is constrained.
Test smaller facility formats (8,000-20,000 sq ft) to validate if a micro model scales better unit economics than a large flagship location.
